content:
The index sets we consider for stochastic processes are almost always linear orders, often have a bottom element, and are roughly in 3 categories: discrete (in which we could reindex by a subset of Int or Nat), countable, and finally uncountable subsets of Real. When proving some results we start with the discrete case and then extend progressively (by first applying the discrete case to finite subsets of larger types).

I'm trying to get a better view of the correct typeclass assumptions in all cases, to see if we could simplify and standardize them. Let's start with the discrete case.

For that case case, Mathlib has results about martingales indexed by Nat and nothing else. The proofs would extend directly to any type that has an OrderIso to a subset of Nat. But what are the right typeclasses to express that? From the results in the file Mathlib.Order.SuccPred.LinearLocallyFinite, we could use [LinearOrder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]. Then we can build succ and pred functions and use what's in that file to get an order iso to either Nat or a subset of the form range n. We could add a new definition to get the iso (or just an embedding) more directly.
But is that the right way to say that something is ordered in that way in Mathlib? I don't know the order part of the library enough to be sure. Or perhaps we should add a typeclass that states that the order iso exists and prove an instance from [LinearOrder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] [OrderBot ι].

I am unsure either. Some cases I would like to see covered:

  • Backwards martingales (index set R−\mathbb R_-R−​ or Z−\mathbb Z_-Z−​);
  • The Brownian Sheet;
  • Stochastic processes indexed by graphs/trees.

Why do we need a linear order? Shouldn't a partial order be enough? (At the price of not having succ and pred, as I understand.)

Another remark about typeclasses: some results about hitting times use [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] (or the variant with a bot [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot ι] [WellFoundedLT ι]), because that's what allows the use of docs#csInf_mem, which states that the infimum of a nonempty set belongs to the set.

Yet another (obvious) remark: The typeclasses you need pretty much depend on the results you are referring to. If you only want to say what a stochastic process is, the index set should not have any structure. If you need to talk about an adapted process, you will need a partial order. If you are talking about a martingale convergence theorem, you will probably need a linear order with some Top. For the definition of hitting times, you probably want a linear order together with some completeness, and be able to extend the intex set by Top if you never hit the set. Etc...

The typeclasses we will need definitely depend on the application but my question here is much more basic. Let's focus on the discrete linear order case. We want to prove results about a process on some index type, and we want those results to apply equally to a process indexed by Nat (as is the case in Mathlib now) or to a process indexed by a finite subset of some other linear order. My question is: what typeclasses do I need on my type to represent those two cases, in a way that works well with Mathlib?

A solution seems to be [LinearOrder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] [OrderBot ι], but for now it's not that convenient because for example Mathlib does not know that it implies [WellFoundedLT ι] (although we can prove it) so the results that we have on hitting times don't apply to that type right now.
So perhaps there is a more canonical way of describing those types, with another list of typeclasses that is equivalent but better integrated with the library.

The proof of WellFoundedLT:

import Mathlib

lemma wellFoundedLT_of_Iic {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] (h : ∀ x : ι, WellFoundedLT (Set.Iic x)) :
    WellFoundedLT ι := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun x ↦ ?_⟩⟩
  have h := (h x).wf.apply ⟨x, le_rfl⟩
  rw [acc_iff_isEmpty_descending_chain] at h ⊢
  contrapose! h
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
  refine ⟨fun n ↦ ⟨f n, ?_⟩, by simpa using hf.1, by simpa using hf.2⟩
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [hf.1]
  | succ n ih => grind

instance {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] : WellFoundedLT ι :=
  wellFoundedLT_of_Iic fun _ ↦ Finite.to_wellFoundedLT

An issue with [LinearOrder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] is that it does not imply InfSet ι (and it should not since that data would conflict with others), so we can't state lemmas involving hitting times.
The typeclasses [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrderBot ι] [LocallyFiniteOrder ι] should be equivalent and contain all the data we need to state theorems, so those are better suited to our goal.
